gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-michroma: Stark, stencil-cut lettering up top, with gaps left open where the curves end. Michroma follows in a contemporary sans that gives each letter wide berth, so a long page reads slowly and spaciously.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-miriam-libre: Approachable from the first line, Miriam Libre carries a lowercase with the stature of cast iron capitals beneath Stencilia's structural, striking display shapes. Stencilia is best loud; the sans-serif is best conversational.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-mochiy-pop-one: Professional in manner, Mochiy Pop One draws every glyph with one stroke width, like laser-cut sheet, under Stencilia's low-contrast heading. And its very large lowercase eye keeps a long passage friendly and steady.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-mochiy-pop-p-one: Mochiy Pop P One sets a sizable lowercase with wide stretches of blank space between letters, drawn in pipe-like strokes. And Stencilia above it brings the structural punch, so the sans below can stay generous and plain.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-montserrat-under: Neutral in temperament, Stencilia's stencil-flat strokes hold the heading, and they are at their best in a bold, display moment. Montserrat Underline handles the reading, with terminals ending at the width they began and a lowercase that looks oversized beside its capitals.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-mozilla-headline: Mozilla Headline reads big-bodied and friendly, with a splayed c terminal. Stencilia is at its best making a striking structural statement, while the plain sans does the approachable, contemporary work of carrying the text.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-mozilla-text: Stencilia's spacious gaps at the curve terminals make it look cut from a template, structural and striking. Mozilla Text responds with tall bodies and flared terminals, so paragraphs look bold and read smoothly.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-nobile: Stencilia opens its curves with spacious gaps at the terminals, which gives it a structural, striking look. Nobile earns the reading work with a minimal gap between x-height and caps, while Stencilia belongs big and short.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-nokora: Cut-open curves and compact ascenders make Stencilia look striking. Nokora fills each line with a thick, dark stripe of lowercase and a wide-open s, so shrinking the heading would waste the stencil's drama.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-kufi-arabic: Noto Kufi Arabic reads modern and clean, with an open, welcoming gap in the c. Stencilia earns its keep when it is big and short, with spacious gaps at its curve terminals.
